direct_answer: Repsol integrates sustainability-related performance into remuneration/incentive schemes by linking annual and long-term variable remuneration to sustainability, decarbonization and energy transition objectives, including for senior leadership. Employee remuneration is reviewed annually by the Executive Committee, the Remuneration Committee and the Board of Directors (which approves it) and is linked to compliance with sustainability and decarbonization objectives [Source 2]. In 2024, ESG objectives were integrated into all business unit objectives with a weighting between 20% and 45% for employees with annual variable remuneration [Source 2]. For the CEO, decarbonization and sustainability objectives represent 25% of annual variable remuneration in 2024 [Source 2], further detailed as 25% linked to sustainability and decarbonization objectives (15% to decarbonization), including 5% tied to increasing installed wind and solar capacity and 10% to developing other low-carbon platforms [Source 5]. Repsol also implemented a Long-Term Incentive (LTI) plan for 2024–2027 applying to all management staff (including the CEO) and other employees, in which 40% of objectives are linked to the energy transition, with metrics including reduction of the Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII), renewable generation capacity (GW) and renewable fuel production capacity (Mta) [Source 5]. Achievement is assessed by the Compensation/Remuneration Committee based on evidence provided, using defined achievement scales with a minimum threshold below which no incentive is generated and a maximum level set at 100% [Source 5]. Governance/approval: the General Shareholders’ Meeting approves the Remuneration Policy for Directors at least every three years; it approved the current policy on 25 May 2023 (for 2023–2026) at the proposal of the Board of Directors, and the Remuneration Committee and Board periodically review the principles and criteria [Source 2]. Additionally, at CEO level, safety incentives are linked to safety indexes and fatalities [Source 4]. Repsol also states that no member of the administrative, management and supervisory bodies has remuneration/incentives linked to specific tax savings parameters [Source 1].
compliance_rationale: The passages provide several GOV-3 elements: key characteristics (annual variable and LTI; thresholds/scales; committee assessment) [Source 5], specific sustainability-related targets/metrics (wind/solar capacity, low-carbon platforms, CII, renewable generation and renewable fuels capacity; safety indexes/fatalities) [Source 5, Source 4], proportions of variable remuneration for the CEO (25% annual variable; 40% of LTI objectives) [Source 2, Source 5], and approval/update level for directors’ remuneration policy (General Shareholders’ Meeting; periodic review by Remuneration Committee and Board) [Source 2]. However, the evidence does not fully and explicitly cover sustainability-linked incentives for all members of the administrative, management and supervisory bodies (beyond the CEO/executive directors and broader employee/management population), nor does it clearly quantify the proportion of variable remuneration dependent on sustainability targets for directors other than the CEO or specify the exact sustainability-linked weightings for the full administrative/management/supervisory bodies.
disclosure_gaps: Explicit description of sustainability-linked incentive/remuneration arrangements for all members of the administrative, management and supervisory bodies (not only CEO/executive directors), including whether non-executive/supervisory members have sustainability-linked pay

Quantified proportion of variable remuneration dependent on sustainability-related targets/impacts for each relevant body/member category (e.g., other executive directors, other board members) beyond the CEO

Clear identification of the full set of sustainability-related targets/impacts used as benchmarks in remuneration policies for administrative/management/supervisory bodies (the passages provide examples but not a complete list)

Clarification of the level at which the terms of sustainability-linked incentive schemes (as distinct from the directors’ remuneration policy) are approved and updated for the different populations covered
key_findings: Remuneration is reviewed annually by the Executive Committee, Remuneration Committee and Board of Directors and is linked to sustainability and decarbonization objectives [Source 2].
In 2024, ESG objectives were integrated into all business unit objectives with a weighting between 20% and 45% for annual variable remuneration populations [Source 2].
CEO: 25% of annual variable remuneration is linked to sustainability/decarbonization objectives; includes 5% for wind/solar capacity growth and 10% for other low-carbon platforms [Source 5].

LTI 2024–2027: applies to all management staff (including CEO) and other employees; 40% of objectives linked to energy transition; metrics include CII reduction, renewable generation capacity and renewable fuel production capacity [Source 5].
Performance assessment uses defined achievement scales with thresholds; assessed by the Compensation/Remuneration Committee based on evidence [Source 5].

Directors’ remuneration policy approval: General Shareholders’ Meeting at least every three years; policy approved 25 May 2023 for 2023–2026; reviewed periodically by Remuneration Committee and Board [Source 2].
CEO safety incentive is linked to safety indexes and fatalities [Source 4].
No remuneration/incentives linked to specific tax savings parameters for members of administrative/management/supervisory bodies [Source 1].
